comparison: Perfect agreement on mouse model generation and validation (C41-C45). Both evaluations find the targeting strategy, sequencing verification, and qPCR validation well-documented and supported. Peer reviewers describe the work as 'well done and good.'

Strong agreement on loss of function evidence (C46-C64, C65-C67). Both evaluations accept the multiple complementary assays demonstrating LOF. OpenEval emphasizes internal consistency across western blots, qPCR, ChIP, and functional assays. Peer reviewers note 'typical loss-of-p53 functions' and 'exceptional level of evidence.'

Agreement on absence of dominant negative effects (C65-C67). OpenEval evaluates this as appropriate negative control comparison in cellular assays. Peer reviewers note similar findings based on heterozygous tumor data, stating 'Y217C may not function as a dominant negative.'

Agreement on chromosomal instability as GOF evidence (C68-C70). Both evaluations accept the increased aberrations in mutant cells compared to WT and null controls. OpenEval emphasizes the critical comparison to both controls; peer reviewers acknowledge GOF properties without concerns.

Agreement on female-specific teratogenic effects (C71-C89). Both evaluations accept the sex bias, exencephaly frequency, and perinatal lethality as well-documented. OpenEval notes extensive breeding data but incomplete mechanistic understanding. Peer reviewers describe findings as 'notable results' showing 'additional, non-cancer related GOFs.'

Agreement on reproductive phenotypes (C90-C95). Both evaluations accept male fertility and dystocia observations. OpenEval notes small sample size (n=2) for dystocia limiting generalizability. Peer reviewers accept findings as part of comprehensive characterization without specific concerns.

Agreement on absence of DNE in heterozygous mice (C96-C98). Both evaluations accept tumor surveillance data showing similar onset and spectrum between Trp53+/YC and Trp53+/- cohorts. OpenEval notes this complements cellular DNE analysis. Peer reviewers explicitly state 'this mutation does not appear to exhibit any dominant-negative effects.'

Agreement on oncogenic GOF through survival and tumor analysis (C99-C105). Both evaluations accept accelerated death, increased aggressiveness, and metastases as strong GOF evidence. OpenEval emphasizes statistical significance and histological evidence. Peer reviewers describe findings as having 'fundamental significance' and 'elevated metastasis.'

Agreement on transcriptomic evidence of LOF/GOF (C106-C109). Both evaluations accept RNA-seq data showing predominantly LOF with some GOF/SOF genes. OpenEval notes technical soundness; peer reviewers state findings are 'indicative of novel target gene activation' and conclusions are 'reasonably well justified.'

Agreement on inflammation as GOF phenotype (C110-C115). Both evaluations accept GO enrichment and qPCR validation of inflammation markers. OpenEval emphasizes complementary evidence from transcriptomics and validation. Peer reviewers note 'novel target gene activation, associated with inflammation.'

Agreement on pathway-level transcriptomic insights (C116-C125). Both evaluations accept GSEA results and NC-NF-κB findings. OpenEval notes mechanistic claims remain speculative requiring validation. Peer reviewers accept findings without criticism, describing work as 'well done' with 'good' quality.

Agreement on supformin rescue experiment (C126-C135). Both evaluations accept the experimental evidence linking inflammation to teratogenic phenotype. OpenEval notes substantial rescue effect but small sample size and need for mechanistic investigation. Peer reviewers describe work as 'well controlled and quite well done' with 'exceptional level of evidence.'

Agreement on X-inactivation analysis (C170-C173, C200-C203). Both evaluations accept qPCR data showing similar defects in mutant and null neurospheres. OpenEval notes this mechanism contributes but doesn't fully explain the more severe phenotype, with modest sample sizes. Peer reviewers acknowledge correlation with decreased Xist expression without concerns.

Agreement on genetic rescue experiments (C204-C214). Both evaluations accept Mdm2/Mdm4 rescue confirming LOF and differential effects on female survival. OpenEval notes small numbers requiring statistical validation and appropriately cautious conclusions. Peer reviewers describe work as 'well-conducted' with 'good' quality.

Agreement on Discussion synthesis of LOF and GOF findings (C136-C159). Both evaluations accept the major conclusions about LOF and GOF being well-supported. OpenEval notes some comparisons are speculative but reasonable. Peer reviewers explicitly accept summary conclusions, describing work as having 'fundamental significance' and 'exceptional level of evidence.'

Partial agreement on integrative inflammation model (C160-C183, overlapping with C178-C179, C181, C194-C197). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting inflammation-tumorigenesis link is supported but mechanistic details remain speculative. Peer reviewers accept overarching conclusions as 'reasonably well justified,' acknowledging 'additional, non-cancer related GOFs' and 'fundamental significance.'

Agreement on broader implications and conclusions (C184-C199, overlapping with C194-C197). Both evaluations accept main conclusion about GOF extending beyond oncogenic effects. OpenEval notes supformin finding is intriguing but preliminary, and some aspects require further investigation. Peer reviewers describe conclusions as 'reasonably well justified' with 'fundamental significance.'

OpenEval evaluates background/literature claims (C1, C15-C40) as appropriately cited and providing context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviewers typically focus on novel findings rather than background literature.
